title: Personal Checking: linking a savings account for overdraft protection transfers
content:
## Scope

This policy governs the overdraft protection link between a Personal Checking account and a PCB savings account, the transfers made through it, and the checking fee each transfer carries. The transfer fee and the daily fee maximum are each checking tier's own published figures.

## Recording or removing the link

A checking account may name one savings account as its overdraft protection source. The link may be recorded only when all of the following hold, each read from the bank's records:

| Condition | Checked against |
|---|---|
| The linked savings account belongs to the same customer as the checking account | The customer recorded on each account |
| The linked savings account is in active status when the link is recorded | The savings account's status |
| The savings tier is designated in the savings product terms as eligible to serve as an overdraft protection source | The savings account's tier |

Removing the link is always allowed.

## Transfers

1. When a debit item would take the checking ledger balance below zero and a link exists, one transfer is made for that item in the exact amount of the shortfall, meaning the amount needed to bring the ledger balance to exactly zero after the item.
2. The transfer is recorded on the checking account against the item it covered, with a matching withdrawal from the savings account; the savings product terms decide whether that withdrawal counts toward the savings withdrawal allowance.
3. A covered item is not an overdraft and carries no overdraft-item fee.

## Retired clause

> **No longer in force:** "the transfer is made only if the savings balance at that moment covers the whole shortfall, and a partial transfer is never made."

This clause is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current coverage basis. The other clauses of this policy remain in force.

## Transfer fee

Each transfer incurs the checking tier's overdraft transfer fee, tied to that transfer, limited to the tier's daily maximum number of transfer fees per account per business day. A tier fee of 0.00 records no fee.

## Worked case: sizing the transfer (hypothetical figures)

A checking account holds 30.00 USD, a link exists, and a debit card payment of 100.00 USD posts. The shortfall is the amount needed to bring the ledger balance to exactly zero after the item: 100.00 less 30.00, which is 70.00 USD. Where a transfer is made for that item, it is one transfer of 70.00 USD, and the checking balance ends the posting at 0.00.

## Basis Q&A

**Q: Can the customer link a savings account held by a family member?**
A: No. The linked savings account must belong to the same customer as the checking account.

**Q: Can a link be recorded to a savings account that is dormant?**
A: No. The savings account must be in active status when the link is recorded.

**Q: Is the covered item also charged an overdraft fee?**
A: No. A covered item is not an overdraft and carries no overdraft-item fee.
